From my limited understanding of things we have two major problems.

The first is that investment bankers are able to use money in commercial banks to place bets on the stock market. Basically what that means is that when you have money in a savings account, your bank is able to invest it in the stock market. A simplified way of thinking of this is that if they lose money on the investment, you lose money in your savings account.

The second major problem is that there is another housing bubble. People like to invest in mortgage bonds since the last bill that people will let go is their mortgage. If you don't pay your mortgage, then you lose your house, and all the money that you put into it. What happened back in 2008 is that banks were offering mortgages that had really low payments for the first two years, but those payments would skyrocket later. They then mixed all of those mortgages into bonds with other non-adjustable rate mortgages and conservative investors (think retirement funds and the like) bought those bonds thinking that they were secure.
